name: stretch-1026-211144
hypothesis: Missed growth: in surviving careers the longest stall is the promotion out of L4. The parent reads 'weakest' as the smallest number. At L4 Output and Network stop at a level high while Skill keeps climbing, so the parent keeps aiming the main action, spare Energy and story preference at Output, which cannot move, rather than at Skill, which is what the next promotion still waits on. Evidence from the champion's 4 completed race digests: 3 spent a year or more at L4 (the fourth reached it only at its final review), and 2 of those reached L5, after 24 and 18 months at L4. In both, Output then sat at 25-26 for 16 and 11 months and Network at 36 for 13 and 5 months, never higher, while Skill climbed from about 57 to 98 and to 90. Two A-grade reviews held with Output and Network at or within two points of that high did not promote (Skill 71 and 70). The two A-grade reviews that did promote came at Skill 98 and 90. The third L4 career ended there with Network flat at 36 for 12 months and Skill 86. In the 8 non-Escalating L4 quarters where Output already sat at 25-26, 6 main actions were aimed at Output (key project 4, Showcase results 1, Report results 1), each with a note naming Output as the gap or the lowest statistic. None lifted Output above 26, and they added at most one point each. Apply for rotation was chosen in 0 of 64 main actions across the 4 completed games. As advertised at L1, the game lists it at Skill +2 and Network +1, against Skill +1 for a key project or a mentorship, and Skill +1 for Skill learning's 2 Energy (lab/reports/first-review-search/*/quarterly-effects.json). So rotation and story choices are the main Skill levers, and Skill learning is a small extra. Skill learning was chosen in 0 Energy phases, including the 2 Clear quarters at the L4 high, whose 6 free points went to Prepare report materials 4, Network maintenance 1 and Health recovery 1. The plateau does not depend on the manual or the actor. Across every state line of the 4 champion digests and the 5 completed Opus ceiling games (lab/reports/teacher-digests/opus-ceiling), no L4 state shows Output above 26 or Network above 36, while L5 states exceed both. The 3 that reached L5 did so after 18-24 months at L4, with Skill 89-97 at their last L4 quarter-end, and the 2 that stayed at L4 ended with Skill 74 and 82. None chose rotation. Why the change captures it: the published bar depends on Skill, Network, Output and level, so once two inputs cannot rise, only Skill can still move a career toward it. The change redefines 'weakest' in the Balance default only. An input that stays unchanged after an action aimed at it is full: it gets no more effort unless it drops, and it is tested again after a promotion. Stories, Energy and the main action go to the inputs still rising, and when only Skill has room the main action is the one listing the largest Skill gain, usually rotation. At L4, Skill rose about 2.5 a month, mostly from stories. Rotation adds one more Skill per quarter than the key project it replaces, free Energy in Clear quarters goes to Skill learning, and story preference turns to capability. This should shorten the L4 stall by about a review in careers that reach L4 early and raise the skill dimension of every long career. It also raises wealth, which is mostly a level gap, through the higher salary and bonus base (published monthly base 0.7 at L4, 1.0 at L5, 1.5 at L6). Below L4 the rule changes little: Skill fills first there, so the inputs left with room are the Network and Output the parent already lifts, and the weak-review and risk rules still override Balance.
change: One edit to Priority 4 (Balance), with matching wording in the turn note. The description, Signals, Priorities 1-3, the Story and Energy bullets and the end-of-run line are the parent's text verbatim. Balance now lifts 'the weakest or falling of Skill, Network and Output, counting only those with room to grow'. A new 'Room' bullet says three things. An input left unchanged by an action aimed at it is full for the level. Spend nothing more on it unless it drops, and test it again after a promotion. Judge the weakest by room left, not by size: at higher levels Output and Network often fill up while Skill is still climbing, and the next promotion then waits on Skill. Because the Story and Energy bullets already say 'the weakest' and allow Skill learning while Health is comfortable, the new definition reaches stories and Energy as well. The main-action bullet adds: if Skill alone has room, take the main action listing the largest Skill gain, usually Apply for rotation, even if that repeats it. The turn note names the 'weakest input with room' instead of the 'weakest dimension'. The manual has 490 words (wc -w, including front matter); the parent has 393.
predicted_behaviour: Notes call an input full once an action leaves it unchanged: at L1 mostly Skill, at L4 Output and Network. At L4 the notes name Skill as the input with room. Outside Escalating quarters and weak-review periods, careers at L4 take Apply for rotation in most quarters once Output and Network are full (parent: 0 of 64 main actions in completed games). Skill learning appears in Clear quarters at higher levels (parent: 0 Energy phases). Prepare report materials and Network maintenance are bought at a full input only to refill a drop. Skill at L4 rises faster than the parent's roughly 2.5 a month, and the move from L4 to L5 comes a review or more sooner than the parent's 18-24 months. More completed careers end at L5, and an early one may reach L6. Completed games end above the parent's level 46, wealth 34 and skill 78. First-promotion timing, Defuse frequency, completion (parent 10 of 12) and risk control (parent 69) stay close to the parent's.
refutation: Refuted, on race games with the same actor, if completion falls below the parent's; if blackouts, trust crises or second-year dismissals rise; or if the first promotion comes later (more games still at L1 after their second review). Any of these means the rule leaked into survival play. Also refuted if completed games do not end with higher level, wealth and skill dimensions than the parent's (46, 34, 78), or do not spend less time at L4. Manipulation check: if no note ever calls an input full and Apply for rotation stays absent at L4 outside Escalating quarters, the text was not executed and the result says nothing about the idea. If rotation does replace Output actions at L4 but Skill growth there does not speed up, the lever is too small and the idea is refuted.
